Motorcycle Recovery in Birmingham

Motorcycles need different handling from cars when they are recovered or transported. A bike has to be secured carefully, particularly if it can't be ridden or has suffered damage. We provide motorcycle recovery across Birmingham and surrounding areas.

Motorcycle recovery is the right choice when:

  • Your bike has broken down
  • The engine won't start
  • You have a flat or damaged tyre
  • The motorcycle has accident damage
  • The bike can't be ridden safely
  • You need to take your bike to a garage
  • You've bought a non-running motorcycle
  • The motorcycle needs moving between locations

GOOD TO KNOW

When Do You Need Motorcycle Recovery?

Motorcycle Breakdown

A mechanical or electrical fault can leave a motorcycle unable to continue its journey. If the bike won't start, or has developed a problem that makes riding unsafe, recovery is the sensible option.

Flat or Damaged Tyre

A puncture or damaged tyre can make a motorcycle unsafe to ride. Rather than carrying on with a damaged tyre, call for recovery and have the bike moved to a safe place.

Accident-Damaged Motorcycle

A collision can damage wheels, handlebars, suspension, brakes and other parts of a motorcycle. Even if the engine still starts, the bike may not be safe to ride.

In this situation, recovery moves the bike away from the accident location and takes it to a garage or another agreed destination.

Non-Running Motorbike

If your motorcycle has been stored for a long time, has developed a mechanical fault or simply won't start, it needs transportation rather than a roadside repair.

Motorcycle Transportation

You may also need recovery for a planned move, such as taking a bike to a specialist garage, collecting one you've just bought or transporting it to another location.

AT A GLANCE

Motorcycle Breakdown Recovery in Birmingham

A breakdown can be especially difficult if you are riding alone or stranded somewhere with little shelter.

Here's what to do:

If anyone is injured or the bike is causing a danger to other road users, call 999 first.

  • Move yourself to a safe place away from traffic where possible.
  • Switch on your hazard lights if the bike is still on the road.
  • Don't try to ride on with a serious mechanical, tyre, steering or braking problem.
  • Call us on 07771 004242 and give us the details listed in the "What Information Do We Need?" section below.

GOOD TO KNOW

Motorcycle Recovery After an Accident

After a collision, motorcycles can suffer damage to components that are vital for safe riding. Common concerns include:

Damaged wheels

Steering problems

Suspension damage

Brake damage

Handlebar damage

Bodywork damage

Engine or mechanical problems

If you are unsure whether your bike is safe, don't ride it. Call us and we'll recover and transport it, whether it's going to a garage, a repair centre or home.

If anyone has been hurt, call 999 before anything else. The bike can wait.

Need accident recovery for a car or another vehicle? See our Accident Recovery Birmingham service.

HOW IT WORKS

How Motorcycle Recovery Works

The exact method depends on the motorcycle, its condition and where it is.

01

Call us on 07771004242 and explain what has happened.

02

Give your location: postcode, road name or another useful reference.

03

Tell us about the motorcycle: make, model and registration if available.

04

Explain the condition: whether the bike starts, rolls and steers, and any visible damage.

05

Confirm the destination: a garage, your home, a repair centre or another agreed location.

06

We arrange the recovery and confirm the details with you before the bike is moved.

Motorcycle Transport to a Garage

If your motorcycle needs mechanical work, you may prefer to have it taken straight to a garage or specialist workshop. This is often the easiest option when:

  • The bike won't start
  • The motorcycle has mechanical damage
  • The tyres are damaged
  • The bike has accident damage
  • You don't want to ride it in its current condition
  • The motorcycle needs a specialist inspection

Give us the garage address when you request recovery, and we'll confirm the collection and delivery details with you.

Call Now: 07771004242 Get A Quote

Non-Running Motorcycle Recovery

A motorcycle doesn't have to be in an accident to need recovery. A non-running bike may need transporting because of:

  • Engine problems
  • Battery failure
  • Electrical faults
  • Fuel-related problems
  • Starting problems
  • Other mechanical faults
  • Long-term storage
  • Accident damage

Tell us whether the bike can roll and steer. It affects how it can be moved safely.

AT A GLANCE

Motorcycle Recovery for Different Types of Bikes

Motorcycles come in many shapes, sizes and designs, so recovery needs vary. We can help with:

Give us the exact type and model when you book, and mention if the bike is particularly heavy or modified.

  • Sports bikes
  • Touring motorcycles
  • Commuter bikes
  • Cruisers
  • Adventure motorcycles
  • Scooters
  • Other road-legal two-wheel vehicles

Before the Recovery Vehicle Arrives

A few simple steps help the recovery go smoothly:

  • Stay somewhere safe while you wait, away from traffic.
  • Take valuables, helmets and loose luggage off the bike if you can do so safely.
  • Keep the keys with you, or tell us if the bike can't be unlocked.
  • Tell us about any fuel or oil leaks, or damage that might make the bike unstable.
  • Have your destination address ready.

Motorcycles need different handling from cars when they are recovered or transported. A bike has to be secured carefully, particularly if it can't be ridden or has suffered damage. We provide motorcycle recovery across Birmingham and surrounding areas.

Motorcycle recovery is the right choice when:

  • Your bike has broken down
  • The engine won't start
  • You have a flat or damaged tyre
  • The motorcycle has accident damage
  • The bike can't be ridden safely
  • You need to take your bike to a garage
  • You've bought a non-running motorcycle
  • The motorcycle needs moving between locations

If a motorcycle has a serious fault or visible damage, riding it away may not be safe. Recovery is the better choice when:

  • The brakes are affected
  • The steering is damaged
  • A wheel is damaged
  • The tyre can't be used safely
  • The motorcycle won't start
  • There is significant accident damage
  • You're unsure whether the bike is roadworthy
